newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Rival Somali faction leaders meet in Mogadishu.
newsitem.headline: Rival Somali faction leaders meet in Mogadishu.

text.p: Rival Somali faction leaders Hussein Aideed and Ali Mahdi Mohamed met on Thursday in a bid to solve the differences between them and bring peace to shattered Mogadishu.
The two leaders met for 90 minutes with committees from both factions and, according to a delegate at the talks, accepted an agenda for negotiations on how to end their power struggle.
It was the fourth meeting between Ali Mahdi, who is based in North Mogadishu and Aideed since he took over at the death of his father as the main faction chief in South Mogadishu last August.

Aideed was elected by supporters as president of Somalia and heads a government rejected by Ali Mahdi and allied factions. Somalia has had no central government and has been torn apart by civil war since 1991.
